tools.name: read_project_structure
tools.description: Return a nested JSON tree of folders and files for a target project. Use this FIRST when you need a quick mental map of an unfamiliar codebase before reading any files. Skips node_modules/.git/dist/.next/build/coverage/.turbo. Max depth 6.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project root to map.

tools.name: get_tech_stack
tools.description: Inspect package.json and report the detected framework (NestJS, Next.js, both, or plain Node), key dependencies with versions, and warnings about notably outdated frameworks. Call this BEFORE choosing how to read an unfamiliar codebase.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project root.

tools.name: find_relevant_files
tools.description: Search a project for files related to a keyword. Looks at filenames, exported class/function names, and variable names. Returns up to 10 ranked matches with a 3-line snippet — use this to LOCATE code before reading whole files.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project root.

tools.name: get_module_summary
tools.description: Summarize the public surface of a folder. Loads every .ts file in the given folderPath (recursive) and reports its exported functions, classes, interfaces, and types plus a one-line inferred summary. Use this to understand a module without reading every file.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project root.

folderPath.description: Folder to summarize, relative to projectPath (e.g. 'src/users').

tools.name: get_architecture_graph
tools.description: Build a stack-aware architecture graph of the project. Picks the right strategy automatically: NestJS @Module decorator graph (with circular-import risks), Next.js route map (App or Pages Router), or a file import graph for plain Node/TS projects. Call this BEFORE making cross-file changes so you understand module relationships.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project root.
